glossary.proenzymes: Inactive forms of enzymes that must be cut or switched on before they work.
glossary.extravasate: To leak out of blood vessels into the surrounding tissues.
glossary.pleural effusion: Fluid collecting between the lung and chest wall.
glossary.pleural effusions: Fluid collections between the lungs and chest wall.
glossary.parenchyma: The working tissue of an organ, as opposed to its supporting framework.
glossary.duodenum: First part of the small intestine, where bile and pancreatic juice enter.
glossary.sulfonamide: A class of antibiotics containing a sulfa group, such as co-trimoxazole.
glossary.anorexia: Loss of appetite (not the eating disorder anorexia nervosa).
glossary.abdominal distension: Swelling or bloating of the abdomen from gas, fluid or bowel dilation.
glossary.bowel sounds: Gurgling noises of gut movement heard with a stethoscope; reduced when the bowel stops moving.
glossary.tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.hypotension: Low blood pressure, usually systolic below 90 mmHg.
glossary.pulmonary oedema: Fluid in the air spaces and tissue of the lungs, causing breathlessness.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.WCC: White cell count, a marker of infection or inflammation.
glossary.WBC: White blood cells; the count rises with infection or inflammation.
glossary.AST: Aspartate aminotransferase, a liver enzyme released when liver (or other) cells are damaged.
glossary.ALT: Alanine aminotransferase, a liver enzyme that rises when liver cells are damaged.
glossary.albumin: The main protein in blood plasma, made by the liver; falls in severe illness.
glossary.urea: Waste product of protein breakdown cleared by the kidneys; rises with dehydration or kidney injury.
glossary.Neutrophils: The most common white blood cells, which fight bacterial infection.
glossary.kPa: Kilopascal, the unit used for blood gas pressures such as PaO2.
glossary.Imrie: Surgeon who co-developed the Glasgow severity score for pancreatitis.
glossary.ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves; good for gallstones and the biliary tree.
glossary.ICU: Intensive care unit, for patients needing organ support.
glossary.stat: Given immediately, as a single dose.
glossary.0.9% saline: Salt solution with the same concentration as blood, used for IV fluids.
glossary.opioid: Strong painkiller acting on opioid receptors, such as morphine.
glossary.hypoxic: Having too little oxygen in the blood or tissues.
glossary.oral feeding: Eating and drinking normally by mouth.
glossary.organ failure: When an organ such as the kidneys or lungs can no longer do its job.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.shock: Inadequate blood flow to the tissues, usually with low blood pressure.
glossary.endoscopic drainage: Draining a fluid collection through a camera passed into the stomach or duodenum.
glossary.communicating: Connected to the pancreatic duct system.
glossary.protein plug: A clump of thickened protein that blocks small pancreatic ducts.
glossary.granulation tissue: New connective tissue and small blood vessels that form during healing.
glossary.epithelial lining: A layer of cells lining a true cyst or organ surface; pseudocysts lack one.
glossary.ascites: Fluid collecting in the peritoneal cavity of the abdomen.
glossary.hypocalcaemia: Low calcium level in the blood.
glossary.ischaemic: Damaged by lack of blood supply.
glossary.parenchymal: Relating to the working tissue of an organ.
glossary.systemic inflammatory response: Body-wide inflammation, with fever, fast heart rate and leaky vessels, triggered by severe injury or infection.
glossary.jaundice: Yellow skin and eyes from raised bilirubin.
